newsitem.title: USA: U.S. layoffs totaled 15,091 in June -- Challenger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. layoffs totaled 15,091 in June -- Challenger.

text.p: U.S. firms laid off 15,091 workers in June, compared with 21,004 in May and 40,163 in June 1996, according to a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
The slowdown in layoffs suggests a labor market short on skilled workers and friendly to job seekers, the report said.

"Just a few years ago, companies bemoaned a costly surplus of employees and job cuts were rampant as a result," John Challenger, executive vice president at the outplacement firm, said in a statement.
"Now just the opposite is true for some firms," he said.
The report said some companies are puttling expansion plans on hold as they strive to fill positions.
"Some companies are even recruiting talented high school students, enticing them with attractive salaries and the promise of specialized on-the-job training," Challenger said.
